title: Rabbi Elazar bar Avina
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Yevamot 63a, saying: “Calamity comes to the world only on account of Israel.” In Berakhot 4b: “Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Avina said: Whoever says ‘Praise of David’…,” etc.; Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar bar Avina, and so it is the reading of Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim. He is likewise mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:5, folio 10. In Bereshit Rabbah 98:2 Rabbi Yehudah speaks in his name — he is Rabbi Yudan, as the statement is cited in Midrash Tehillim 31:7. At the beginning of Pesikta deRav Kahana we find Rabbi Tanchum his son-in-law, and Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on “I have come into my garden,” reads Rabbi Menachem his son-in-law.

notes.text: תהלה לדוד is rendered “Praise of David,” preserving the distinction from a מזמור. The bar-versus-said-that emendation, Yehudah/Yudan identification and Tanchum/Menachem sons-in-law remain Hyman’s supplied claims. Folio 10 has no side supplied.

The inspected Yevamot 63a names Elazar bar Avina and explicitly says that calamity comes only on account of Israel. The exact Ein Yaakov/Dikdukei Soferim readings and the Yehudah/Yudan and Tanchum/Menachem relations remain Hyman’s supplied claims.
